content.title: About
content.content: The bean burrito with no cheese is a Mexican dish consisting of a soft wheat tortilla filled with seasoned beans, rice, vegetables, and sauce. Cheese is omitted, making it lighter and suitable for those avoiding dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where large wheat tortillas were used.
Beans in burritos are often cooked with tomatoes, onions, and spices for a rich flavor.
Leaving out cheese makes the dish more vegan‑friendly, especially when plant‑based substitutes are used.
Burritos are commonly served with guacamole, salsa, and lime for extra zest.
In the United States, burritos have become a fast‑food staple and appear on many chain restaurant menus.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide a substantial amount of protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from beans and vegetables supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Omitting cheese reduces saturated fat content, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Beans and whole‑grain tortillas supply B1, B6, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: The dish offers iron, magnesium, and potassium, supporting energy levels and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Prepared sauces can be salty; monitor sodium intake to avoid excess.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gas in sensitive people; soaking them before cooking helps reduce this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the burrito hot, cut in half for easy handling. Serve with salsa, guacamole, or a squeeze of lime. Vegans can add tofu or plant‑based cheese for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Frozen burritos keep well for up to 3 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
